Working mainly in the studio with his favoured maple Hohner Telecaster, Prince’s solo-crafting was largely instinctual. “He was a master of the neck by the time he passed away, for sure. Back in the early days he relied on some patterns on the neck that he’d always orient to. They worked to his muscles, and how his fingers moved. On Computer Blue there’s a little section where I have to follow him and play exactly what he’s playing. Up to this day, I find that an awkward fingering pattern. My fingers don’t work as fluidly as his did. I still have to use extra brain power to get that final triplet feel at the very end of that pattern.” [Lisa Coleman] With her textured, chordal washes, rhythmic chops and occasional fretboard flourishes, Wendy chose a Rickenbacker 330 as her guitar of choice. It would become a key part of her signature until it was infuriatingly stolen from her. We ask Wendy what attracted her to the Rickenbacker: “Well, because at the time they were offered to us.
